unused-toolchains.rust.name: Unused Rust toolchains
unused-toolchains.rust.what: Versions of the Rust compiler that rustup installed and that nothing on this Mac points at: not rustup's default, not an override, not a project's toolchain file.
unused-toolchains.rust.if-removed: The toolchain's folder goes to the Trash. A project, a script or an editor that asks for this exact version gets an error until it is installed again.
unused-toolchains.rust.comes-back: Yes, with one command and a download of a few hundred megabytes. Components and targets you added to it must be added again.
unused-toolchains.node.name: Unused Node versions (nvm)
unused-toolchains.node.what: Versions of Node.js that nvm installed and that nothing on this Mac points at: not nvm's default or another alias, not a project's .nvmrc, .node-version or .tool-versions.
unused-toolchains.node.if-removed: The version's folder goes to the Trash with every global package installed with it. An editor set to this exact Node stops finding it.
unused-toolchains.node.comes-back: With one command and a download. Global packages you installed with it must be installed again.
unused-toolchains.enabled.label: Unused toolchain versions
unused-toolchains.enabled.description: Finds Rust toolchains that nothing on this Mac points at. Each goes to the Trash and comes back with one command.
unused-toolchains.node-versions.label: Node versions (nvm)
unused-toolchains.node-versions.descript: Also finds Node versions nvm installed that nothing points at. Off by default: global tools installed with a version go with it.
unused-toolchains.reason.rust: Nothing on this Mac points at it. Last opened or changed on {date}. To get it back: {command}.
unused-toolchains.reason.node: Nothing on this Mac points at it. Last opened or changed on {date}. To get it back: {command}.
unused-toolchains.left-out.special: It holds a connection a running program may be using, so it is kept.
unused-toolchains.left-out.not-yours: Some of it belongs to the system or another user, or is locked, often after a command run with sudo. Removing it needs an administrator.
unused-toolchains.left-out.partial-scan: Some folders could not be read, so a project there might use this version.
unused-toolchains.left-out.default-unkno: Fresher could not read which version is the default, so it keeps every version.
unused-toolchains.left-out.pin-unknown: A version file in your folders could not be read, so Fresher cannot tell which versions are used.
